state.requirements: A Japanese-language personal life-plan simulator MVP. Users sign in with Google before seeing any financial forms. They enter hypothetical monthly take-home income, living costs, initial cash and investment assets, start month, horizon (1-600 months), assumed return and inflation. Living costs are funded first; remaining surplus is split between saving and investing with synchronized numeric input and slider. Editable dated income/cost changes and one-off events. Show cash, investment and total asset line charts, final balances, first shortage month/amount and matching monthly detail tables. Stop lines at shortage, never zero-fill after termination. Compare up to three named cases with different assumptions and line styles as well as colors. Account-only server save/load/update/delete, visible unsaved state, stale results warning, confirmation dialogs, error/expired-session/conflict recovery. Desktop settings/results should be easy to compare; mobile is one column. Accessible labels, keyboard focus, contrast, readable Japanese and dense numerical data. Calm and trustworthy without promising investment outcomes; no product recommendations. The design is for an authenticated working application, not a promotional landing page. No real personal financial data is supplied. Public design samples are hosted at https://sample.chartd.net; their visual metadata is provided in the catalog. Preserve functional clarity when adapting a sample to forms/charts/tables/comparison.
